fixes.explanation: The rulers were "…captured without a bow." and the fugitives "…were captured together, having fled to a distant place." Think about that. They fled, even to a distant place, and still ended up captured. So the running ended in captivity.

Battle sounds close, but look at verse 2. The slain "…did not die by the sword, nor were they killed in battle." Verse 3 says the rulers were captured without a bow, and the fugitives were captured too. So the verse lands on captivity.

Verse 7 says, "Your choicest valleys are full of chariots, and horsemen are posted at the gates." So the best land is packed with chariots, and the gates have horsemen posted there. A gate is the front door of a city, and I'd say that door has company.

Verse 10 says, "You counted the houses of Jerusalem and tore them down to strengthen the wall." They tore houses down to strengthen the wall. Imagine counting your own street just to see how much of it you can pull down.
